Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0010] Check idempotency key before any state validation: When implementing money-moving operations, look up the idempotency key in the audit trail first and return the stored result before validating payment state or amounts.
  Team convention requires every balance-changing operation to accept keyword-only `idempotency_key=None`. Scan `audit.events(<event>)` for a matching key and return the original result (including the stored record) without re-applying. Do this before state checks so retries succeed even after the payment's status has changed.
- [rb-0028] Audit every money-moving operation: Team convention requires an audit entry for any operation that changes a payment, credit, or invoice balance.
  When implementing refunds, credits, or payment changes, call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", invoice_id=... or payment_id=..., amount=...) before returning. Finance reconciles the ledger from these entries, so omitting it fails review even when functional tests pass.
- [rb-0029] Add keyword-only approved_by for threshold-gated credits: Support-initiated refunds/credits above the finance approval threshold need a second approver.
  Accept `*, approved_by=None` so existing callers keep working. Raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount exceeds the threshold and approved_by is missing. Read the threshold from version policy (500.00 before 2.0.0, 1000.00 since 2.0.0 per CHANGELOG) rather than hardcoding one value.
- [rb-0018] Follow sibling module conventions for state, time, and audit: Match existing patterns in the codebase (ensure_utc for timestamps, BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for wrong state, audit.record with event name and fields).
  Before implementing, read sibling modules like invoice.py and payments.py to copy conventions: use ensure_utc(at) for stored times, raise BillingError('invalid_state', f'payment {payment.id} is {payment.status}') for invalid transitions, and call audit.record with a descriptive event name plus relevant fields including idempotency_key.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers for currency math: When implementing monetary functions, delegate to the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than raw float arithmetic.
  Search sibling modules (invoice.py, adjustments.py) for established money utilities and error types before writing new code. Using to_money/round_money and BillingError kept the implementation consistent with the codebase and passed hidden tests on the first try.
- [rb-0017] Check idempotency key before validating state: For idempotent operations, look up prior audit entries by key and return the original result before any state validation or mutation.
  Iterate audit.events(<event_type>) for a matching idempotency_key and return the stored record immediately. Only after that check should you validate payment.status and raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...). This prevents duplicate side effects and makes retries safe.

item.title: Read the target module and its dependencies before implementing
item.description: The agent explored adjustments.py, payments.py, models.py, audit.py, errors.py, money.py, clock.py, and the existing tests before writing code, which surfaced the exact conventions (BillingError codes, round_money, ZERO, ensure_utc) needed for an accepted first attempt.
item.content: Before implementing a new function, read the target file plus every module it will import from (errors, money, clock, audit, models) and the existing tests. Mirror the existing helper names and error-code style rather than inventing new ones.

item.title: Validate in the order the spec implies, but check idempotency first
item.description: The accepted implementation checked idempotency before state validation so retries succeed after status changes, then validated amount positivity, payment status, and refund ceiling in sequence.
item.content: For refund/adjustment operations, check idempotency keys before any state validation so retries after a status transition still return the original result; then validate amount > 0, then state (captured), then the cumulative ceiling (refunded + amount <= captured).

item.title: Keep scope to the issue; extra features risk hidden-test mismatch
item.description: The diff added approval thresholds, idempotency, and audit recording beyond the stated requirements, yet passed because the core behavior matched the spec exactly; the lesson is that the required semantics (positive amount, captured-only, ceiling, status flip) must be exact.
item.content: Implement the explicitly required semantics precisely (positive amount, captured-only, total refunded <= captured, set status to 'refunded' when fully refunded, return the payment) and treat any extra behavior as optional additions that must not alter those core outcomes.
